content:
maria: heads up — page retirement rate for pool12/card3 just jumped, row_remap_count spiking over the last 10m :eyes: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/pool12-card3?orgId=1
infra-bot: ALERT: GPU_PAGE_RETIRES_HIGH on pool12/card3 (severity: warning) — value=78, rate=+3.2x over 10m
aj: can you paste the last Xid / dmesg lines? curious if it's correlated with ECC or soft errors
maria: grabbing logs now, short snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=9123, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568234] NVRM: GPU page-retire: retired pages=120, remap_events=42
[ 1234.570000] kernel: GPU_MAINT: page migration triggered for device 65:00
```
devon: that Xid 79 + page-retire pattern usually means growing DRAM errors; we've seen the same precursor before. recommend draining this GPU node and scheduling replacement.
leo: quick impact calc — pool12 has 16 gpus, losing card3 reduces available capacity by ~6%. If we drain during low traffic window (02:00-05:00 UTC) we should be fine.
anika: +1 to drain. can we reroute latency-sensitive qps to pool9? Is autoscaler going to compensate?
aj: autoscaler will pick up but we should proactively migrate long-running job assignments. I'll patch scheduler affinity for models with strict latency.
sre-oncall: assign a ticket and flag Dedicated customers on this pool. also please run vendor memory diagnostics (memtestG) and collect ECC counters.
maria: created ticket HW-12345, assigned to hw-ops, ETA vendor triage tomorrow. attaching ECC counters snapshot:
```
GPU 65: ECC_CORRECTABLE: 1342
GPU 65: ECC_UNCORRECTABLE: 4
GPU 65: page_retire_count: 120
```
devon: 4 UCEs is worrying — try forcing a page-scrub and re-run workload. command I usually use: `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 65` (note: requires node maintenance).
leo: can we avoid a full reboot? maybe try draining just the pods on the GPU and reprovision a spare from pool13 as a replacement before reboot.
anika: spare capacity in pool13 is limited but we can preempt noncritical batches. I'll mark two batch queues as preemptible.
aj: ops checklist so far:
- mark node cordoned
- kubectl drain pool12-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- migrate long-running models to pool9/pool13
- collect memtest logs and ECC counters
- open vendor case (HW-12345)
- schedule maintenance 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC
please react with :thumbsup: when done.
maria: starting the cordon now, will post back when drain completes. :hammer_and_wrench:
infra-bot: ACTION: cordon initiated for pool12-node-3 by maria at 1802503240
maria: pods draining — currently 12/15 evicted, ETA ~4m
leo: FYI capacity planner: moving two small embeddings jobs to pool9, should keep latency OK
anika: preemption set for batch-qa and batch-embeds queues
devon: after drain, run `nvidia-healthmon --dump-errors --since=24h` and attach output to HW ticket
aj: also add metric alert to detect page_retire_count delta > 50 in 1h so we catch similar regressions earlier
sre-oncall: good call. tagging INC-2026 for internal tracking and adv-notify customers list.
maria: drain completed at 1802503425, node cordoned and removed from LB pools. rebooting GPU now to try a soft reset.
infra-bot: NOTE: node pool12-node-3 removed from routing (drain) by maria at 1802503425
maria: quick post-reset check shows page_retire_count still increasing but at a slower rate. leaving node out of rotation until vendor confirms. attaching health dump link: https://storage.redwood.example/hw-dumps/HW-12345/dump1.txt
leo: status: replacement ordered if vendor confirms bad DIMs. capacity impact minimal after migrations.
anika: follow-up: schedule a short postmortem and update runbook with the `page_retire` threshold we used. we should standardize: when remap_rate > 2x baseline for 10m -> auto cordon candidate.
devon: +1 to runbook change. i'll draft the PR.
maria: thanks all — monitoring continues, I'll update ticket and this thread once vendor triage completes. :white_check_mark:
